subtheme: A Christmas Angel Tree Gift Tag
description: A wish label guides a donated present for a Christmas giving project.
cardDescription: A wish label guides a donated present for a Christmas giving project.
focus: The setting is a Christmas Angel Tree Gift Tag. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Small label attached to an item
Tall plant with a woody trunk
Giving help to people in need
Give part of something to others

answerNotes.ANGEL: Angel means a heavenly messenger in the Bible stories. Decorative angel figures are representations rather than the story characters themselves.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
answerNotes.GIFT: A gift is something given, rather than sold. A tag identifies the recipient; wrapping protects or decorates the present.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.
answerNotes.TOY: A toy is made for play. A miniature model can be a toy, a hobby project, or a display depending on its use.
answerNotes.COAT: A coat is an outer garment. Its lining is inside, while the collar and pockets are visible features outside.
answerNotes.WRAP: Wrap means put a covering around something. Paper is common for parcels and shop goods, while cloth can also be a wrapping material.
answerNotes.RIBBON: A ribbon is a narrow fabric strip. A looped bow and a straight trailing tail are different parts of a tied ribbon decoration.
answerNotes.SHARE: Share means give part of something to others. In a meal setting it can concern food rather than dividing property or money.
answerNotes.CHRISTMAS: Christmas customs vary between households. These scenes include ordinary decorations and sharing activities as well as clearly labeled Christian stories elsewhere.

answerNotes.COOKIE: American English uses cookie for a small sweet baked treat. In Britain, many such treats are called biscuits.
answerNotes.LID: A lid is a removable cover. On a cooking pot it helps contain heat and steam; on a jar it closes the opening.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.GIFT: A gift is something given, rather than sold. A tag identifies the recipient; wrapping protects or decorates the present.
answerNotes.RIBBON: A ribbon is a narrow fabric strip. A looped bow and a straight trailing tail are different parts of a tied ribbon decoration.
answerNotes.CHRISTMAS: Christmas customs vary between households. These scenes include ordinary decorations and sharing activities as well as clearly labeled Christian stories elsewhere.
answerNotes.SWEET: Sweet describes flavor, not temperature or texture. A food can be sweet and cold, or sweet and warm.
answerNotes.BAKE: Baking uses dry heat in an oven. Boiling instead cooks food in bubbling liquid.
answerNotes.STAR: A star can mean a distant sun or a pointed decorative shape. Christmas ornaments represent the shape rather than an actual celestial object.

Location written on a mailed envelope
Colored liquid used by a pen
Letters delivered by the postal service
Public board with words or symbols

answerNotes.CARD: Card can mean a printed greeting or a playing piece. An envelope points to a greeting; a deck or suit points to a game.
answerNotes.LIST: A list records items in order. Checking off a purchased item is different from changing the price or quantity of it.
answerNotes.ADDRESS: An address tells where mail should go. The recipient's name identifies the person, while the street, city, and postal code locate the destination.
answerNotes.STAMP: Stamp can mean a postage label or a tool that leaves an ink impression. A mailed letter and a craft project use different senses.
answerNotes.ENVELOPE: An envelope encloses a letter. The destination goes on its front; the message stays inside.
answerNotes.NAME: A name identifies a person or thing. In a family album, adding names helps later readers recognize the people pictured.
answerNotes.PEN: A pen writes with ink. A pencil uses graphite, which can usually be removed with an eraser.
answerNotes.CHRISTMAS: Christmas customs vary between households. These scenes include ordinary decorations and sharing activities as well as clearly labeled Christian stories elsewhere.
answerNotes.SIGN: Sign can be a public notice or the action of writing a name. Check whether the clue describes an object or asks for a verb.

answerNotes.CAROL: A carol is a seasonal song. In these Christmas scenes it concerns singing rather than a person's name.
answerNotes.SHEET: Sheet can name paper, bed linen, or a flat baking pan. The scene tells whether the material is paper, cloth, or metal.
answerNotes.SONG: A song has words and a melody. In the familiar-title puzzles, ordinary definitions help even when a reader does not remember the recording.
answerNotes.PAGE: A page is one side of a book's paper. A single physical leaf normally has two pages, front and back.
answerNotes.PRINT: A print can be an image or an impression. In snow, it is the mark left by a foot or shoe rather than words on paper.
answerNotes.PIANO: A piano sounds when keys cause hammers to strike strings. In silent-film theaters, a live pianist sometimes supplied the accompaniment.
answerNotes.VOICE: A voice is the sound produced when someone speaks or sings. A speaker is the device that reproduces the sound on a call or recording.
answerNotes.CHRISTMAS: Christmas customs vary between households. These scenes include ordinary decorations and sharing activities as well as clearly labeled Christian stories elsewhere.
